**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — a breaking change affects import ID format for one resource type; confirm this template does not use it before applying.

### Breaking changes
- `resource/aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record: Change the format of the import ID from `domain_name,dnssec_key_id` to `domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key`. This is acceptable in a minor version because AWS no longer return DNSKEY flags and delegation signer records can no longer reliably be found by domain name and key ID` — only matters if this template manages or imports `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` resources. This RDS pipeline template does not appear to use Route 53 domain delegation signer records, but confirm no such resource exists anywhere in the Terraform configuration before upgrading.

### Variables
- none — the `.env.example` provided is empty, and the notes name no provider-level variables, environment variables, or `.tfvars` entries that changed. The provider version constraint itself lives in `01-providers.tf`: `version = "~> 6.69.1"`, which would need to be widened to allow `6.70.0` (e.g. `~> 6.70.0` or `>= 6.69.1, < 7.0.0`) — this is a required edit to the compose/provider pin, not an upstream variable change.

### Data and dependencies
- none found in the notes. No RDS, database, or companion-service version requirement is introduced or raised in this range. (The enhancement `resource/aws_rds_cluster: Add `publicly_accessible` argument` is from 6.69.0, already in the current baseline, not part of this move.)

### Before applying
- Edit `01-providers.tf` to relax the version constraint from `~> 6.69.1` to permit `6.70.0` (e.g. `~> 6.70.0`), since Terraform provider pessimistic constraints with a patch-level pin (`~> 6.69.1`) only allow `6.69.x`, not `6.70.x`.
- Search the Terraform configuration and state for any `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` resource. If present, treat existing state/import IDs as needing re-import after upgrade, per the breaking change note.
- Run `terraform plan` after the provider upgrade and before `apply`, as normal practice, to confirm no unexpected diffs from the `aws_guardduty_*` default-entry fix or other behavioural changes.

- Release notes for `v6.69.1` (2026-10-15), given as the baseline — read in full.

## Upstream changes 1.17.1 -> 1.18.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — the upgrade requires coordinated action (Local sandbox auth token, Agent Backend run-protocol compatibility, database migrations) even though no un-pinned companion-service version is introduced.

### Breaking changes
- `/runs` now accepts only the new request format: *"`/runs` now accepts composition v2 and rejects v1 requests. Existing session snapshots are converted on read and saved as v2; old runtimes cannot read newly saved v2 snapshots."* The Agent Backend and the API/worker images must move together — mixing a 1.17.1 Agent Backend with a 1.18.0 API (or vice versa) breaks runs.
- The Local sandbox requires a non-blank auth token and a matching runtime image: *"The `1.17.1` runtime image does not support the new `--require-auth-token` flag; deploy the matching `1.18.0` Agent Backend and Local sandbox images."* This template's `DIFY_AGENT_LOCAL_SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN` is already mandatory (`:?set in .env`), so the token itself is not new here — but the 1.18.0 Agent Backend/local-sandbox images now *enforce* it in a way 1.17.1 did not.
- Old Agent-specific AskHuman tool and deferred resume path are removed: *"historical Agent forms no longer resume execution, while shared Workflow Human Input nodes remain supported."* Any in-flight or historical Agent-form resumes will not work after upgrade.
- Legacy workflow/resume consumers must be retired before new traffic is admitted (point 3 of the upgrade guide) — rolling partial upgrades of workers is not safe.
- Nginx (bundled) now overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` and Compose enables forwarded-header handling: *"Bundled Nginx replaces `X-Forwarded-For` with its resolved client address, and Compose enables forwarded-header handling... If a load balancer or Cloudflare sits before Nginx, configure trusted real-IP handling there."* This template puts Traefik in front of the bundled nginx, so this is directly applicable — verify Traefik is configured to forward real client IPs correctly or rate-limiting will bucket all visitors together.

### Variables
- `DIFY_AGENT_LOCAL_SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN` — already required by this template's compose file (`:?set in .env`), so not a new requirement here, but note must be delivered the way the notes specify: *"Setting it only in a service env file is insufficient."* This template sets it via `x-app-env` / compose `environment:`, which should satisfy that — no action needed, just confirm it is non-blank.
- `GRAPH_ENGINE_MAX_WORKERS` — new fixed-worker-count variable, default `10`; `GRAPH_ENGINE_MIN_WORKERS`, `GRAPH_ENGINE_SCALE_UP_THRESHOLD`, `GRAPH_ENGINE_SCALE_DOWN_IDLE_TIME` are removed ("no longer used"). None of these appear in the .env.example shown, so nothing to edit, but if an operator set any of the removed three by hand they are now dead.
- `PASSWORD_PEPPER` — new, defaults empty: *"Leave it empty on an existing unpeppered installation to preserve logins."* Not present in .env.example; leave unset. Do not add it casually — the notes warn *"Setting, changing, or removing the pepper invalidates existing password hashes."*
- `RESPECT_XFORWARD_HEADERS_ENABLED` — notes say bundled Compose "explicitly enables it for API/WebSocket services behind Nginx." This template's `.env.example` and compose file do not set this variable for `api`/`api_websocket` at all — confirm whether it needs to be added given Traefik → nginx → api/api_websocket topology, per the proxy-boundary review point above.
- `KNOWLEDGE_FS_ENABLED` (and related KnowledgeFS variables) — new, default `false`. Not present in .env.example; no action unless Agent Knowledge Base is wanted, and the notes are explicit that this needs a separate service/database not provided by this compose file.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` — new, default `false`. Not present in .env.example; no action needed unless opting in.
- Removed: `GET /console/api/apps/{app_id}/feedbacks/export` endpoint — not an env var but check any external integration calling it directly.
- `UV_CACHE_DIR` — the template's .env.example already sets `UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/.uv-cache`, so the removal of the upstream baked-in default does not affect this template.

### Data and dependencies
- 22 schema/data migrations plus two head merges, ending at `b9d3f7a5c102`. Must run before new workers start: *"Apply the complete migration chain before starting the new workers."* `MIGRATION_ENABLED=true` is already the default in this compose file for `api`/`worker`/`worker_beat`, so this is handled automatically on container start — no manual command required unless migrations are run out-of-band.
- Weaviate: notes state the bundled Weaviate in 1.18.0 moves from `1.39.2` to `1.39.13`, "a patch update within 1.39." **This template still pins Weaviate at `1.27.0`** (`DIFY_WEAVIATE_IMAGE_VERSION:-1.27.0`), i.e. it never completed the staged 1.17.1 Weaviate upgrade path (`1.27.0` → `1.39.2`) that the 1.17.1 baseline notes required. The 1.18.0 release notes explicitly say: *"If coming from a version that still runs Weaviate 1.27, complete the [1.17.1 staged Weaviate upgrade] first."* This is a pre-existing gap from the 1.17.1 baseline, not something this range introduces, but it blocks a safe 1.18.0 Weaviate bump and must be resolved by hand before or alongside this upgrade — the compose file's own Weaviate pin has not been updated to track either 1.17.1's or 1.18.0's bundled Weaviate version.
- KnowledgeFS (opt-in): requires "its separate database and migrations" and is not shipped by this compose file at all — correctly left disabled by default. No action needed unless the operator wants the Beta feature.
- `b9d3f7a5c102` and the Classic Dataset upgrade worker: "apply `b9d3f7a5c102` before restarting API/workers/Beat" — covered by the standard migration-enabled startup, not a separate manual step for this template.

### Before applying
- Back up the Postgres database, Weaviate volume, uploaded files (`dify-app-storage`), and Agent sandbox volumes (`dify-agent-sandbox-home`, `dify-agent-sandbox-workspace`) before upgrading, per the notes' upgrade guide point 1.
- Upgrade `api`, `web`, `local-sandbox`, and `agent-backend` images together to 1.18.0 — this compose file's comment already enforces this convention ("The api, web, local-sandbox and agent-backend images are one Dify release: move them together or not at all"), so set all four `DIFY_*_IMAGE_VERSION` variables (or the single defaults in `x-images`) to `1.18.0` together.
- Resolve the outstanding Weaviate version gap first: this template is still on `1.27.0`; before or alongside this upgrade, complete the staged Weaviate upgrade to at least `1.39.x` referenced in the 1.17.1 notes, then separately decide whether to track Weaviate `1.39.13` as referenced by 1.18.0. Do not jump directly from `1.27.0` to `1.39.13` in one step — the notes call 12-minor-version skips unsupported.
- Confirm `DIFY_AGENT_LOCAL_SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN` in `.env` is a real high-entropy value (not the example placeholder) before restarting, since the new images enforce it.
- Drain in-flight workflow/agent runs and stop old workers before starting new ones, rather than doing a rolling restart, per the "retire old workflow consumers" guidance.
- Verify `PASSWORD_PEPPER` is left unset/empty (it is not present in this template's files, so the default empty behavior applies — no action needed, just don't add it casually).
- Review whether `RESPECT_XFORWARD_HEADERS_ENABLED` needs to be set for `api`/`api_websocket` given the Traefik → nginx proxy chain, since the upstream Compose default behavior described in the notes is not visibly configured in this template's files.
- After upgrading, re-import/re-index any documents affected by the extraction fixes if desired (optional, not required for the stack to function).

- `1.18.0` release notes (full body, including Upgrade Guide, Environment Variables, and Database Migrations sections) — read in full for the 1.17.1 → 1.18.0 range.
- `1.17.1` release notes — read only as the stated baseline, per instructions, to separate already-true requirements (e.g., the staged Weaviate upgrade) from changes introduced by this range.
